subject.title: Expose structured progress metrics in hook events for plugin-based live progress cards

question: Should OpenClaw add structured progress metrics to existing plugin hook events, and if so which runtime source owns step totals, percentages, ETA, and terminal metrics across run producers?
rationale: The implementation is feasible, but this would define public Plugin SDK semantics for progress and could mislead users if tool counts are treated as completion percentages without a maintainer-approved source of truth.

options.title: Define a narrow metrics contract
options.body: Add optional metrics only where the runtime can produce authoritative values, document absent unknowns, and cover the affected producers with focused tests.

options.title: Keep current hook payloads
options.body: Leave plugins to derive progress from existing tool and lifecycle events, accepting text-only or phase-only progress cards until a stronger source exists.

options.title: Design a separate progress event
options.body: Introduce a dedicated progress event or agent-event projection instead of attaching percentages to tool and terminal hooks.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow metrics contract
recommendation.body: Add optional metrics only where the runtime can produce authoritative values, document absent unknowns, and cover the affected producers with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history trail for public hook contract and hook-context changes points to `vincentkoc`, and this decision affects Plugin SDK semantics.
